title: Stefanos Fragkoulis
text:
Hello World, I’m Stefanos!
I am a Biologist and PRINCE2-certified Project Manager. I combine a strong scientific foundation with advanced data science skills to bridge the gap between complex research and technical execution.
Currently, I manage workflows and coordinate panel committees at the Hellenic Foundation for Research and Innovation (HFRI). Moving forward, I am actively seeking remote Bioinformatics, Data Science, or Technical Project Management roles within the EMEA region where I can dedicate the majority of my time to writing code, building pipelines, and analyzing data.


Beyond the Screen
When I am not managing panels or writing code, you will usually find me outdoors walking, running, or hiking. I train in multiple martial arts—including Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Kyokushin Karate, and Kickboxing—and I proudly serve as a volunteer Samaritan cadet with the Hellenic Red Cross.

title: Technical Publications
text:
Fragkoulis, S. & Nikolaou, C. Analysis of the evolutionary history of eukaryotic genes in relation to their spatial arrangement in the eukaryotic nucleus. (in preparation)
Antinero, A., Printzi, A., Kourkouta, C., Fragkoulis, S., Mazurais, D., Zambonino-Infante, J.L., & Koumoundouros, G. (2023). The role of starter diets in the development of skeletal abnormalities in zebrafish Danio rerio (Hamilton, 1822). Journal of Fish Diseases, 46, 697–705 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/jfd.13779
Summary: Different early-stage diets significantly alter the incidence of skeletal deformities—such as scoliosis and swimming-induced lordosis—in larval zebrafish without affecting overall growth or survival, underscoring the potential for nutritional control of skeletal anomalies in finfish aquaculture.
Fragkoulis, S., Kourkouta, C., Geladakis, G., Printzi, A., Glaropoulos, A. & Koumoundouros, G. (2022). Recovery of Haemal Lordosis in European Seabass Dicentrarchus labrax (Linnaeus 1758). Aquaculture Journal, 2, 1-12 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/aquacj2010001
Summary: Tracking European seabass from the juvenile to harvest stages reveals that the majority of fish with swimming-induced haemal lordosis naturally recover a normal body shape, a finding supported by new morphometric indices designed to help commercial hatcheries screen for skeletal abnormalities.
Fragkoulis, S., Kerasovitis, D., Batargias, C. & Koumoundouros G. (2021). Body-shape trajectories and their genetic variance component in Gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata L.). Scientific Reports 11, 16964 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-95726-9
Summary: Tracking the morphological development of Gilthead seabream from juvenile to adult stages reveals a substantial additive genetic component in both their final body shape and the rate of shape change, offering a heritable basis for improving selective breeding programs in aquaculture.
Printzi, A., Kourkouta, C., Fragkoulis, S., Dimitriadi, A., Geladakis, G., Orfanakis, M., Mazurais, D., Zambonino-Infante, J.L., & Koumoundouros, G. (2021). Balancing between Artemia and microdiet usage for normal skeletal development in zebrafish (Danio rerio). Journal of Fish Diseases, 44, 1689–1696 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/jfd.13487
Summary: The transition rate from live feed to a dry microdiet significantly impacts the incidence of skeletal abnormalities, growth, and survival in larval zebrafish, demonstrating that a more gradual dietary transition is crucial for ensuring normal skeletal development.
Fragkoulis, S. & Koumoundouros G. (2021). Simple morphometrics for predicting lordosis-induced deviations of body shape in reared Gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata L.). Journal of Fish Diseases, 44, 1265-1267 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/jfd.13384
Summary: This study demonstrates that a simple, non-lethal predictor angle (PrAn) measured from three external landmarks can effectively quantify and predict the severity of haemal lordosis and its ultimate impact on the body shape of reared Gilthead seabream at harvest.
Fragkoulis, S., Economou, I., Moukas, G., Koumoundouros, G. & Batargias, C. (2020). Caudal fin abnormalities in Gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata L.) have a strong genetic variance component. Journal of Fish Diseases, 43, 825-828 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/jfd.13180
Summary: By examining Gilthead seabream larvae, this study reveals that caudal fin abnormalities possess a substantial additive genetic component with moderate heritability, suggesting that targeted selective breeding could be an effective strategy to decrease the incidence of these deformities in commercial aquaculture.
Printzi, A., Fragkoulis, S., Dimitriadi, A., Keklikoglou, K., Arvanitidis, C., Witten, P.E. & Koumoundouros, G. (2019). Exercise-induced lordosis in zebrafish Danio rerio (Hamilton, 1822). Journal of Fish Diseases, 98, 987-994 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/jfb.14240
Summary: Subjecting zebrafish to continuous swimming exercise rapidly induces dose-dependent haemal lordosis, establishing a reliable and welfare-compatible model for studying skeletal abnormalities in post-embryonic vertebrates.
Fragkoulis, S., Printzi, A., Geladakis, G., Katribouzas, N. & Koumoundouros, G. (2019). Recovery of haemal lordosis in Gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata L.). Scientific Reports 9, 9832 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-46334-1
Summary: Tracking Gilthead seabream during the sea cage on-growing phase reveals the first evidence, that haemal lordosis can naturally recover over time, restoring a completely normal external body shape and vertebral column in a significant portion of affected fish.
Fragkoulis, S., Batargias, C., Kolios, P. & Koumoundouros, G. (2018).Genetic parameters of the upper-jaw abnormalities in Gilthead seabream Sparus aurata. Aquaculture, 497, 226-233 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aquaculture.2018.07.071
Summary: While gross, externally visible jaw deformities in Gilthead seabream larvae lack significant heritability, specific underlying internal skeletal abnormalities exhibit a significant genetic component, demonstrating that precise phenotypic scoring is essential for effective selective breeding programs.
Crespel, A., Zambonino-Infante, J.L., Mazurais, D. Koumoundouros, G., Fragkoulis, S., Quazuguel, P., Huelvan, C., Madec, L., Servili, A. & Claireaux, G. (2018). The development of contemporary European sea bass larvae (Dicentrarchus labrax) is not affected by projected ocean acidification scenarios. Marine Biology, 164, 155 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00227-017-3178-x
Summary: Chronic exposure to projected ocean acidification scenarios had minimal adverse effects on the early development of European sea bass larvae and unexpectedly reduced skeletal deformities, suggesting these fish possess an innate physiological resilience to future hypercapnic conditions without needing to mobilize specific defense mechanisms.
Fragkoulis, S., Christou M., Karo, R., Ritas, C., Tzokas, C., Batargias, C. & Koumoundouros, G. (2016). Scaling of body-shape quality in reared gilthead seabream Sparus aurata L. Consumer preference assessment, wild standard and variability in reared phenotype. Aquaculture Research, 48, 2402-2410 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/are.13076
Summary: By integrating consumer preferences to develop a morphological quality scale, this study demonstrates that both the origin of the fish (Wild versus Reared) and the specific rearing environment significantly alter the body shape and key morphometric traits of Gilthead seabream.
Fragkoulis, S., Paliogiannis, H., Kokkinias, P., Chiers, K., Adriaens, D. & Koumoundouros, G. (2016). Saddleback syndrome in European sea bass Dicentrarchus labrax (Linnaeus, 1758): anatomy, ontogeny and correlation with lateral-line, anal and pelvic fin abnormalities. Journal of Fish Diseases, 40, 83-95 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/jfd.12494
Summary: Anatomical and ontogenetic analysis of saddleback syndrome in reared European sea bass reveals that the condition originates from severe marginal finfold abnormalities during the early flexion stage and strongly correlates with additional fin and lateral line defects.

title: Academic Monographs
text:
Doctoral Dissertation | Biology
Allometric growth patterns of body shape in Gilthead sea bream (Sparus aurata Linnaeus, 1758). Normal phenotype and skeletal deformities
DOI: http://hdl.handle.net/10442/hedi/48656
Summary

This research utilized geometric morphometry, X-ray imaging, and individual pit-tagging to longitudinally track the external morphology and skeletal deformities of reared gilthead sea bream from the juvenile stage to harvest size.
The study revealed that normal body shape undergoes significant biphasic allometric growth, while also documenting the first evidence that severe deformities like haemal lordosis can naturally recover through vertebral remodeling or counter-balanced kyphosis.
Ultimately, demonstrating this morphological plasticity during the on-growing period provides valuable predictive tools for enhancing selective breeding programs and improving the quality of commercial aquaculture products.

Keywords: External morphology, Allometric trajectories, Skeletal biology, Geometric morphometry
Master’s Thesis | Applied Bioinformatics and Data Analysis
Analysis of the evolutionary history of eukaryotic genes in relation to their spatial arrangement in the eukaryotic nucleus
DOI: https://repo.lib.duth.gr/jspui/handle/123456789/22090
Summary

This research investigated the three-dimensional spatial reorganization of the genome, specifically Radial Positioning (RP), during the transdifferentiation of B-lymphocytes into macrophages.
By analyzing distinct time points and evolutionary gene origins, the study revealed significant chromosomal relocation where nuclear positioning strongly correlates with both a gene’s functional role and its phylogenetic age.
Ultimately, the findings demonstrate that cellular reprogramming requires more than just a transcriptional shift, relying heavily on a comprehensive spatial restructuring of the genome to establish a new cellular identity.

Keywords: Systems biology, Genome architecture, Bioinformatics
Master’s Thesis | Environmental Biology
Sources of phenotypic variation in reared Gilthead sea bream. Morpho-anatomical abnormalities, variability of normal phenotype and heritability estimations
DOI: https://elocus.lib.uoc.gr/dlib/3/f/0/metadata-dlib-1424950701-864372-31568.tkl
Summary

This research investigated the phenotypic variance of reared sea bream, examining how different rearing conditions affect skeletal abnormalities in larvae and overall body shape in adults.
By developing novel semi-quantitative scales and conducting parentage analysis, the study revealed significant heritabilities for both specific external jaw deformities (\(h^2 = 0.115 \pm 0.041\)) and distinct adult morphological traits.
Ultimately, establishing these quantitative metrics for early ontogenetic stages minimizes environmental noise, providing highly heritable morphological targets to improve future selective breeding programs in aquaculture.

Keywords: Skeletal abnormalities, Heritability, Plasticity
